info.text:
In September 2021, El Salvador became the first country to make bitcoin legal tender and gave $30 in bitcoin to every adult who signed up for its Chivo wallet. This video explains why a country that has used the US dollar since 2001 tried bitcoin, what surveys found about who actually used it, how the government built a stash of about 7,825 coins (as of Nov 4, 2026), and how a $1.4 billion IMF loan approved in February 2025 came with a 2025 reform that made accepting bitcoin voluntary for businesses. Along the way we chart remittances as a share of El Salvador's economy and work through the math on the government's holdings and the IMF loan per person.

News and education, not financial advice.
